A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same DyReMe study. Their main texts, equations, figures, tables, and complete appendices support reliable comparison, including matching relocated prompts and renumbered results.

before.justification: v1 reports original benchmark comparisons, diversity and ablation experiments, evaluations of 12 LLMs, human annotations, and generator self-recognition experiments.

after.justification: v2 retains these empirical results and adds GPT-5 evaluations, English DDXPlus results, a judge-swap experiment, and original-question human ratings.

M1.justification: DyGen's generation components and EvalMed's scoring procedures are retained. Algorithm 1 renames PGDOPTIMIZE to VALIDATEANDREFINE, matching the existing validator-refiner loop. Added extraction and diagnosis-selection details do not establish an underlying procedure change.

E1.justification: v2 adds evaluation on English DDXPlus in Section 4.3 and Table 2; v1 used its Chinese translation. DxBench, Dxy, RJUA, and the diagnostic task remain covered as before.

E2.justification: Table 1 adds GPT-5, expanding the challenge comparison from 10 to 11 LLMs. The human-quality study adds original questions as a comparison baseline. DyVal2, Self-Evolving, and the separate 12-model EvalMed panel are retained.

E3.justification: Appendix E adds a protocol replacing GPT-4.1 with GPT-5 as judge for three evaluated models. Table 4 adds ratings of 30 original questions from a disjoint, unpaired set. Existing Chinese evaluation sample sizes, temperatures, and main metrics remain unchanged.

E4.justification: v2 substantially broadens validation through evaluator-dependence testing, English-language generalization, and a human-quality control using original questions. These address additional reliability questions beyond the retained component ablations, extensibility analysis, self-recognition experiment, and case studies.

E5.justification: Both versions report ten 80% bootstrap samples, one-sided t-tests, benchmark standard deviations, and Gwet's AC1. New English p-values accompany added results; no changed uncertainty-estimation procedure, seed policy, or increased repeated-run count is documented.

E6.justification: Several result groups are added: GPT-5 scores of 73.76 on static benchmarks versus 67.67 on DyReMe, English GPT-4o scores of 85.10 versus 77.18, GPT-5-judged results, and original-question quality averaging 3.97 versus the retained generated-question score of 3.89. Appendix B.5 revises the highly consistent scoring-point count from 24 to 25. Existing Table 1 rows and Figure 4 results are retained.

T1.justification: The diagnostic-task definitions, Equations 1–7, and appendix entropy/diversity formulations are unchanged. No new theorem, proof, formal assumption, or mathematical derivation is introduced.

C1.justification: The abstract and introduction narrow broad clinical-realism claims toward controlled, scalable stress testing under clinically grounded confounders. The central DyReMe contribution, its two components, and the claim that current LLMs exhibit diagnostic weaknesses remain.

C2.justification: v2 explains rumor injection as a controlled stress test rather than a representation of ordinary consultation frequency. Section 6 adds specific workflow and prospective-validation boundaries, replacing broader-task future directions. Appendix E newly interprets preserved benchmark ordering as evidence of evaluator robustness.

D1.justification: v2 adds a DyReMe code-release link and planned six-month refresh schedule, identifies the retrieval services, and clarifies diagnosis extraction, normalization, and top-diagnosis selection. Direct repository links for the two dynamic baseline implementations are removed, although their use remains documented.

R1.justification: The cited literature is substantially expanded and revised across the introduction, evaluation discussion, and references. Section 2 newly positions CRAFT-MD, MedKGEVal, and ClinDEF as complementary clinical-evaluation frameworks, distinguishing their interaction/workflow focus from DyReMe's controlled diagnostic stress testing.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, related-work discussion, and several experimental passages undergo extensive rewriting. Appendix E becomes 'Reliability Checks' with separate generator and evaluator discussions. Most methodological mathematics and appendix prompt text remain intact.

P2.justification: v2 adds Tables 2, 4, 10, and 11 and a GPT-5 row in Table 1; Table 10 redisplays existing results. Figure 4 and several appendix displays are relocated. Existing plots and the overall two-column layout are retained.

improvement.justification: English validation, the original-question human baseline, clearer scope qualifications, and code-access information improve support and transparency. Gains are limited by new inconsistencies: Table 11's DeepSeek-V3 scores of 71.68 and 59.11 imply a 17.54% decline, while it reports 11.68%, and Section 6 still claims exclusively Chinese evaluation. The net improvement is modest, with the judge-robustness quantification requiring clarification.
